H1.statement: On information-bound tasks, E helps; K, M, A1, P1 and P2 do not
H1.falsified_if: K gives a significant gain on leakage-free information-bound instances
H1.test: exact one-sided McNemar superiority (E vs baseline) + Newcombe paired TOST (K, M, A1, P1, P2 vs baseline)

H2.statement: On reasoning-bound tasks, K helps; E (restating held evidence), M and A1 do not
H2.falsified_if: Restated evidence gives a gain as large as K at matched delta, not explained by easier presentation (checked with P1)
H2.test: exact one-sided McNemar superiority (K vs baseline) + Newcombe paired TOST (E, M, A1, P1, P2 vs baseline)

H3.statement: On communication-bound tasks, M helps; K and same-kind private E do not
H3.falsified_if: K alone lifts inner-product-like accuracy significantly above chance at fixed message budget
H3.test: exact one-sided McNemar superiority (M vs baseline) + Newcombe paired TOST (K, E, A1, P1, P2 vs baseline), on comm_parity and comm_ip

H4.statement: A1 gives no gain on any family
H4.falsified_if: A significant A1 gain on any family
H4.test: Newcombe paired TOST (A1 vs baseline) per family; falsifier: exact McNemar superiority of A1

H5.statement: The A2 gain equals the gain from the same delta compute given to one agent
H5.falsified_if: Multi-agent A2 significantly beats single-agent + delta compute
H5.test: Newcombe paired TOST (A2 vs A2_single_ref) per family; falsifier: exact McNemar superiority of A2

H6.statement: Information-bound error never falls below the Fano floor
H6.falsified_if: Error significantly below the floor (audited for leakage first)
H6.test: one-sided binomial test of error below the Fano floor in each (T, p) cell that could reject (zero errors would give p < alpha); Holm within each model

H7.statement: Inner-product-like splits stay near chance until about n/2 bits; parity-like splits jump at 1 bit
H7.falsified_if: Inner-product-like accuracy rises steadily from the first bits
H7.test: inner product: change-point vs linear by instance-grouped cross-validated log-likelihood, plus slope test; parity: accuracy at L=1 at least 90% of its ceiling, ceiling >= 0.7

H8.statement: Mixed tasks show a positive interaction between the two matching interventions

H9.statement: The blind diagnostic names the binding ceiling well above chance on held-out constructed tasks

sample_sizes.method: ceilings power on pilot runs (see analysis.sample_size_method)
sample_sizes.pilot_estimate: about 1,200 paired instances per cell for the equivalence tests, from the October 2026 pilot after removing the floor-scoring artefact; to be recomputed with `ceilings power` on a pilot run under this design

exclusion_rules: info-family instance solved at baseline beyond chance (leakage)

analysis.superiority: exact one-sided McNemar test on discordant pairs (binomial, p = 0.5)
analysis.equivalence: TOST by inverting the Newcombe (1998, method 10) paired-difference interval at level 1 - 2 alpha; the p-value is the smallest alpha at which the interval lies inside (-margin, +margin)
analysis.non_binary_outcomes: paired t-tests with the standard error floored at 0.5/n (only if replicates are averaged)
analysis.multiple_comparisons: Holm, two families per model: support tests (every pre-registered test of H1-H5) and falsification tests (each hypothesis's own falsifier); each (family, arm, reference) comparison is counted once per family
analysis.support_rule: a hypothesis is supported for a model when every one of its support tests rejects after Holm
analysis.contradiction_rule: a hypothesis is contradicted for a model only by its own pre-registered falsifier (after Holm, with a gain above the margin); H2 additionally requires the restated-evidence gain to be at least the K gain and P1 not to help. A matching arm that fails to help leaves the hypothesis inconclusive, never contradicted
analysis.not_evaluable_rule: a model's verdict on a hypothesis is 'not evaluable' (with reasons) when the calibration gate failed for a family it needs, a required arm is missing, or any of its tests has fewer paired instances than sample_sizes.per_cell
analysis.across_models: a hypothesis is contradicted if at least 2 evaluable models are contradicted, otherwise supported if at least 2 evaluable models are supported, otherwise inconclusive; 'not evaluable' if no model is evaluable. The same rule applies to H6 and H7, each model judged on its own sweep cells
analysis.gains_reporting: paired cluster bootstrap intervals over instances; gain versus realized cost is also reported
analysis.calibration_gate: difficulty search (calibrate): screening rule, baseline within 5 points of chance with the tolerance on the estimate's 95% interval and the full fix >= 90%; confirmation (prepare, on fresh instances, rule 'confirm'): baseline equivalent to chance within +/-0.05 by two one-sided exact binomial tests at alpha 0.05, and the full fix's one-sided 95% exact lower bound >= 0.90; chance is the instance's own (2^known / 2^k in the information family); info leakage: baseline correct with p >= 0.9
analysis.difficulty_rule: per model, the grid is searched from easy to hard; info and comm take the hardest passing setting, reason the easiest; the search stops when the full fix misses 90% (no harder setting can pass) or, for reason, at the first pass
analysis.cost_matching: each arm's mean added tokens within +/-5% of the target delta on the pilot instances, by choosing the arm's strength (largest that fits) and topping up with neutral filler
analysis.sample_size_method: ceilings power: per comparison, n for TOST under a true difference of 0 and n for McNemar at the pilot gain, from pilot discordance, alpha planned as alpha/k within each Holm family; per_cell is the maximum over the equivalence tests of families whose gate passed
analysis.secondary_outcome: the team's aggregated probability on the true answer (p_true), reported alongside accuracy
analysis.ties: a majority-vote tie not broken by mean probability is broken with the run's own seed

design.labels: true answers balanced across instances (each option the truth equally often, in a seeded order)
design.information_family: host table listed in a seeded random row order per instance; optional `known` attributes stated up front (partial-information setting); Fano floors use the full bound h(Pe) + Pe log2(M-1) >= H - B
design.communication_families: every arm reasons at depth 'medium' (baseline included); K starts above that depth
design.K: strength is a depth plus how many of the 4 answer samples reason at it (e.g. 'medium:1'); the others answer at the family's baseline depth; candidates in cost order, matched to the target
design.A2_single_ref: one agent whose reasoning depth is chosen by cost matching to A2's target (not A2's own strength topped up with filler)
design.ablations: each harness option is cost-matched in its own run root; `ceilings run` refuses an arms table matched under different harness options

run_plan.decided: 2026-10-26, by the researcher, to fit a budget of about $500
run_plan.models: the 10 in configs/openrouter.json (10 developers), each pinned to one hosting provider
run_plan.main_grid: all 9 arms at the medium delta, n = 850 paired instances per cell, for every (model, family) whose confirmation gate passes
run_plan.delta_curves: all three delta levels (small, medium, large) on 3 models, chosen after calibration as the models with the most passing families, at most one per developer; a documented deviation from FR-009 for the other 7
run_plan.gate: prepare --gate confirm on about 300 fresh instances per family
